status: source-reviewed proposal; not executed or adopted
scope: One selected-engine Player component-group capability check after the World Liquor respawn slot; no production player replacement

selected_sources.variable_max_auto_step: absent in base and component groups; this is not a capability failure

prior_evidence: No same-Player/version/group result found in the bounded existing capability records or memory lookup; mob examples do not establish Player support
input_boundary: Construct the disposable QA player definition from the exact selected vanilla source, retaining all other fields; declare the whole test-only overlay in native evidence.
The group uses the documented default0.5625 plus0.5 for ordinary/controlled stepping; the actual Player baseline is measured, not inferred from a missing JSON component.
Keep jump_prevented_value at its documented baseline for this ordinary-block capability check. Do not change jump, movement, camera, collision or native attributes elsewhere.
No added Player properties, no synthetic Script component or movement-vector override, no teleport or impulse inside measured native-step windows.
one_player_observations: Baseline: genuine Survival Player native movement toward the same full block without High Heels or the QA group; record input, position, velocity and jump state.
Enable only the QA native group; repeat the same movement and determine whether the Player steps onto the full block without jumping or teleporting.
Disable the QA group and verify return to the original stepping behavior on the same actor.
Compare actual jump arcs before and during the group on the same level floor; record velocity/displacement, without assuming auto-step changes jump force.
Keep native input/delivery failures inconclusive; a missing getComponent result or a successful event alone does not decide capability.
relationship_to_current_fix: The passable/liquid false-positive repair remains a separate necessary owner fix. The prepared exact Player.tryTeleport keepVelocity test remains on the actual T module version; this proposal is not evidence for or against that method.
adoption_boundary: A successful QA result would still require the existing public Core composer and functional-owner descriptor, preserving the CBS-owned production Player definition. Do not add a Tavern player.json override or private integration gameplay implementation.
